sentences.en: Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 哈喽，哈喽，哈喽，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 制作的英语学习播客《English Learning for Curious Minds》，在这里，你可以聆听精彩的故事，了解世界上稀奇古怪、美妙绝伦的事物，同时还能提升英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today it’s the start of another three-part mini-series, this time on the theme of citizenship and identity.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天我们开始一个新的三集迷你系列，这次的主题是公民身份与认同。

sentences.en: In part one, today’s episode, we are going to talk about the case of Italy and the country’s recent referendum on easing the rules on citizenship.
sentences.zh: 在第一集，也就是今天的节目中，我们将探讨意大利的情况以及该国最近关于放宽公民身份规则的全民公投。

sentences.en: In part two, we’ll talk about the Windrush scandal, a recent British political scandal in which tens of thousands of people, mostly from former British colonies in the Caribbean, found themselves treated as outcasts in their own country.
sentences.zh: 在第二集里，我们将讨论“疾风世代丑闻”（Windrush scandal），这是一起近期轰动英国政坛的丑闻，数万名主要来自加勒比地区前英国殖民地的人，发现在自己的国家被当成了边缘人。

sentences.en: And in part three, we will talk about the battle between the Mediterranean island of Malta and the European Union, a battle for the right to sell citizenship.
sentences.zh: 而在第三集，我们将讨论地中海岛国马耳他与欧盟之间的博弈，这是一场关于出售公民身份权力的争夺战。

sentences.en: OK then, let’s get right into it, and ask ourselves what makes an Italian.
sentences.zh: 好了，那我们马上切入正题，来探讨一下究竟是什么造就了一个意大利人。

sentences.en: Now I want to start this episode by telling you something about me.
sentences.zh: 我想在节目的一开始，先和大家分享一些关于我自己的事情。

sentences.en: It’s not a secret, and I’m certainly not ashamed of it.
sentences.zh: 这并不是什么秘密，我也绝不为此感到羞耻。

sentences.en: But it’s not something that everyone knows, and it’s not something that’s immediately obvious.
sentences.zh: 但并不是所有人都知道这件事，而且它也不是一眼就能看出来的。

sentences.en: It’s not something that you would guess by looking at me.
sentences.zh: 这不是那种光看我的外表就能猜到的事情。

sentences.en: It’s not something that you would guess by hearing my voice.
sentences.zh: 也不是那种听我的声音就能猜到的事情。

sentences.en: It’s not something that you would guess if I told you about my parents, my brother and sister, my cousins, or anything about my childhood.
sentences.zh: 如果我向你讲述我的父母、兄弟姐妹、表亲，或者我的童年往事，你也是猜不到的。

sentences.en: It’s this: I am Italian. I have an Italian passport; I am, legally speaking at least, as Italian as Giorgio Armani or Sophia Loren.
sentences.zh: 事实是这样的：我是意大利人。我有一本意大利护照；从法律意义上讲，我和 Giorgio Armani 或 Sophia Loren 一样，是个地道的意大利人。

sentences.en: And in fact, I am more Italian than tens of thousands of people who were born and raised in Italy, who speak no language other than Italian, know no other country but Italy, but are not Italian citizens.
sentences.zh: 事实上，比起成千上万在意大利出生长大、只会说意大利语、除了意大利不了解别的国家却没有意大利国籍的人来说，我甚至更像个意大利人。

sentences.en: I have Italian citizenship through marriage.
sentences.zh: 我通过婚姻获得了意大利国籍。

sentences.en: My wife is Italian, which allowed me to become an Italian citizen.
sentences.zh: 我的妻子是意大利人，这让我得以成为意大利公民。

sentences.en: There are a few technicalities to this–different waiting periods depending on whether you live in Italy or not, and whether you have children, and then you have to pass a language test and not have a criminal record–but in my case at least, I was eligible to become an Italian citizen after three years of marriage, despite not living or working in Italy or having any connection to Italy apart from my wife.
sentences.zh: 这里面有一些技术细节——根据你是否住在意大利、是否有孩子，等待的时间会有所不同，此外你还必须通过语言测试且没有犯罪记录——但至少对我而言，在结婚三年后，尽管我不住在意大利、不在意大利工作，除了我妻子之外与意大利没有任何联系，我依然有资格成为意大利公民。

sentences.en: Interestingly enough, for my wife, the reverse is not true; it is significantly more difficult and expensive for her to become a UK citizen than it is for me to become an Italian citizen.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，对于我妻子来说，情况恰恰相反；她想要获得英国国籍，要比我获得意大利国籍困难得多，成本也高得多。

sentences.en: Now, especially for the Italians listening to this, you might think this is perfectly fair, you might think it is grossly unfair, but it is the law.
sentences.zh: 现在，特别是对于正在收听节目的意大利听众来说，你可能会觉得这非常公平，也可能会觉得这极不公平，但这就是法律。

sentences.en: As you will know, a country has the right to set its laws on who is entitled to citizenship.
sentences.zh: 如你所知，一个国家有权制定关于谁有资格获得公民身份的法律。

sentences.en: At birth, citizenship is typically granted based either on jus soli, where a child becomes a citizen of the country they were born in, or jus sanguinis, where the child becomes a citizen by blood, because their mother or father was a citizen, or some combination of the two.
sentences.zh: 在出生时，公民身份通常基于“出生地原则”（jus soli），即儿童成为其出生国家的公民；或是基于“血统原则”（jus sanguinis），即儿童因其父母一方是公民而通过血统成为公民，亦或是这两种原则的某种结合。

sentences.en: Most countries in the Americas, like the US, Mexico and Brazil, prioritise jus soli, where anyone born in the country is a citizen, regardless of the citizenship of their parents, while most European countries–like Italy and the UK–are much more restrictive, and prioritise citizenship through descent; you become a citizen through ancestry, through blood.
sentences.zh: 美洲的大多数国家，如美国、墨西哥和巴西，都优先采用出生地原则，即在境内出生的人无论其父母国籍如何皆为公民；而大多数欧洲国家——比如意大利和英国——则限制得多，优先考虑通过世袭获得公民身份；你通过祖先、通过血统成为公民。

sentences.en: And globally, most countries also offer some form of pathway to citizenship, even if you weren’t born in that country or have no ancestry in that country.
sentences.zh: 在全球范围内，大多数国家也都提供某种形式的获取公民身份的途径，即使你并非在该国出生，或在该国没有血统渊源。

sentences.en: Typically, this is through either marriage, as it was in my case, or an extended period of time spent living in that country.
sentences.zh: 通常，这要么通过婚姻（就像我的情况一样），要么通过在该国居住较长的一段时间。

sentences.en: But there are other ways, such as the topic we’ll cover in part three of this mini-series: paying lots of money.
sentences.zh: 但还有其他方式，比如我们在本系列第三部分将要讨论的主题：花一大笔钱。

sentences.en: In the case of Italy, the country has relatively loose restrictions when it comes to acquiring citizenship through ancestry or marriage, but much stricter rules regarding citizenship through residency.
sentences.zh: 就意大利而言，该国在通过血统或婚姻获得公民身份方面的限制相对宽松，但在通过居住权获得公民身份方面的规则则要严格得多。

sentences.en: Or to translate that into plain English, I was able to become an Italian citizen after just three years of being married, but someone who was born in Italy and had lived in Italy their entire life but whose parents weren’t Italian citizens, well unless they had applied for citizenship between their 18th and 19th birthdays, they might find it very difficult to become Italian.
sentences.zh: 或者用大白话来解释，我仅仅结婚三年就能成为意大利公民，但如果某人出生在意大利并在意大利度过了一生，可他们的父母不是意大利公民，那么除非他们在18岁到19岁生日之间申请入籍，否则他们可能会发现自己很难成为意大利人。

sentences.en: And it was this that was one of the key focuses of a referendum put to the Italian public in early June this year.
sentences.zh: 正是这一点，成为了今年6月初提交给意大利公众的一场公投的核心焦点之一。

sentences.en: The referendum actually had 5 questions, with 4 of them relating to labour laws, but the most important question was one on citizenship.
sentences.zh: 这场公投实际上有5个问题，其中4个与劳动法有关，但最重要的问题是关于公民身份的。

sentences.en: The public was asked to vote on whether the time limit for non-EU citizens living in Italy to become Italian citizens should be reduced from 10 years to 5 years, which would bring it in line with other European countries, such as France, Germany, and the UK.
sentences.zh: 公众被要求投票决定，居住在意大利的非欧盟公民获得意大利国籍的年限是否应该从10年缩减至5年，这将使其与法国、德国和英国等其他欧洲国家保持一致。

sentences.en: Now, as a quick side note, Italy has quite a strong tradition of holding referendums, and an equally strong tradition of those referendums failing to reach the required turnout rate of 50%.
sentences.zh: 顺便提一句，意大利有着相当浓厚的举行公投的传统，但同样有着未能达到50%法定投票率要求的悠久传统。

sentences.en: So they are often used more like political tools to express unhappiness at government policy and direction rather than genuine vehicles of political change.
sentences.zh: 因此，公投往往更多地被用作表达对政府政策和方向不满的政治工具，而不是真正带来政治变革的途径。

sentences.en: So, who exactly was pushing for this referendum?
sentences.zh: 那么，究竟是谁在极力推动这次公投呢？

sentences.en: And perhaps more importantly, why now? Well, the short answer is: the political left, trade unions, and a coalition of pro-immigration and civil rights groups.
sentences.zh: 或许更重要的是，为什么偏偏是现在？简短的回答是：政治左翼、工会，以及一个由支持移民和民权组织组成的联盟。

sentences.en: Italy, like much of Europe, has seen significant immigration over the past 30 years, and many of the children of these immigrants, these second-generation Italians, have grown up in Italy, speak only Italian, go to Italian schools, and consider themselves Italian in every way.
sentences.zh: 和欧洲大部分地区一样，意大利在过去30年中见证了显著的移民潮，这些移民的许多孩子，也就是所谓的第二代意大利人在意大利长大，只说意大利语，上意大利学校，并且在各方面都认为自己是意大利人。

sentences.en: But, in the eyes of the law, they're not; they are foreigners.
sentences.zh: 但是，在法律眼中，他们不是；他们是外国人。

sentences.en: For years, there have been growing calls to make it easier for these people to obtain Italian citizenship, to officially recognise their Italian identity, not just socially or culturally.
sentences.zh: 多年来，一直有越来越呼吁简化这些人获得意大利国籍的手续，以便在官方层面上承认他们的意大利身份，而不仅仅是在社交或文化层面上。

sentences.en: Supporters of the reform argued that the existing system is unfair and out of touch with modern Italy.
sentences.zh: 改革的支持者认为，现行体制是不公平的，并且与现代意大利脱节。

sentences.en: After all, they say, if someone has lived in Italy for most of their life, paid taxes, gone to school, speaks the language fluently, and calls Italy home, doesn’t this make them Italian?
sentences.zh: 毕竟，他们说，如果一个人在意大利生活了大半生，纳税、上学、能流利地说当地语言，并把意大利当成家，这难道不能让他们成为意大利人吗？

sentences.en: And this question of citizenship has also become wrapped up in wider debates about Italy’s ageing population and its future workforce.
sentences.zh: 而关于公民身份的这个议题，也与关于意大利老龄化人口及其未来劳动力的更广泛讨论交织在了一起。

sentences.en: The country, as you may know, has one of the lowest birth rates in Europe, with 1.24 births per woman, and hundreds of thousands of young people leaving for other countries.
sentences.zh: 如你所知，该国的生育率是欧洲最低的国家之一，每名女性生育1.24个孩子，同时有数十万年轻人远走他乡。

sentences.en: Its population is ageing and shrinking, with a quarter of the population aged over 65 and just 12% under the age of 14.
sentences.zh: 它的人口正在老龄化且不断萎缩，四分之一的人口年龄超过65岁，而14岁以下的儿童仅占12%。

sentences.en: Its economy increasingly depends on migrant labour to keep key sectors running, everything from agriculture to elderly care to logistics.
sentences.zh: 其经济越来越依赖外来劳动力来维持关键部门的运转，从农业到老年护理再到物流，无所不包。

sentences.en: From this perspective, making it easier for long-term residents and their children to become citizens isn’t just a question of fairness, so the argument goes; it’s also a practical solution to a looming demographic crisis.
sentences.zh: 从这个角度来看，正如人们所争论的那样，让长期居民及其子女更容易获得公民身份，不仅是一个公平问题，也是应对迫在眉睫的人口危机的一个切实解决方案。

sentences.en: In short, Italy needs more people, and many argue that it should start by giving citizenship to people who are already there.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，意大利需要更多的人口，许多人认为，它应该从给予已经生活在那里的人公民身份开始。

sentences.en: But, as you might expect, not everyone agrees.
sentences.zh: 但是，正如你所料，并非所有人都赞同这一点。

sentences.en: Opposition to the reform comes mainly from the right, where political leaders have consistently argued against any loosening of the rules around citizenship.
sentences.zh: 对改革的反对主要来自右翼，那里的政治领袖一直坚决反对任何放松公民身份规则的做法。

sentences.en: For these parties, citizenship is not simply an administrative label, a matter of residency, or a tool to secure economic growth.
sentences.zh: 对这些政党而言，公民身份不仅仅是一个行政标签、居住地的问题，或是促进经济增长的工具。

sentences.en: It’s about identity, history, culture — and, in their eyes, about protecting what it means to be Italian.
sentences.zh: 它关乎身份、历史、文化——在他们眼中，它关乎捍卫意大利人的本质。

sentences.en: They argue that Italian identity is something inherited through blood and tradition, not simply acquired by living in the country for a few years and being able to correctly identify the difference between an espresso macchiato and a cappuccino.
sentences.zh: 他们认为，意大利身份是通过血统和传统传承下来的，而不是仅仅通过在该国居住几年、能够正确分辨意式浓缩咖啡（espresso macchiato）和卡布奇诺的区别就能获得的。

sentences.en: There’s also the question of control. Like in much of Europe, in Italy, immigration has been one of the most polarising political issues for years, particularly since the European migrant crisis of 2015.
sentences.zh: 这里还存在一个控制权的问题。和欧洲大部分地区一样，在意大利，移民问题多年来一直是两极分化最严重的政治议题之一，特别是自2015年欧洲难民危机以来。

sentences.en: The right argues that relaxing citizenship rules could act as a pull factor, encouraging more immigration, and that the system should remain strict to prevent abuse and protect the country’s “social cohesion”.
sentences.zh: 右翼认为，放松入籍规则可能会起到一种“磁吸效应”，鼓励更多移民涌入，因此系统必须保持严格，以防范滥用并保护国家的“社会凝聚力”。

sentences.en: And beyond ideology, there is, of course, political calculation.
sentences.zh: 除了意识形态之外，当然还有政治算计。

sentences.en: The issue of citizenship divides public opinion quite neatly along political lines.
sentences.zh: 公民身份这一议题沿着政治阵线将公众舆论清晰地划分开来。

sentences.en: For the right, opposing reforms like this is a way to mobilise their base, to present themselves as defenders of tradition, of the nation, of Italian values, however you might define those.
sentences.zh: 对右翼而言，反对这样的改革是动员其基本盘的一种方式，把自己包装成传统、国家和意大利价值观的捍卫者——无论你如何定义这些价值观。

sentences.en: And while supporters framed this reform as modern, inclusive, and pragmatic, opponents presented it as rushed, dangerous, and as something that could erode and dilute Italian identity.
sentences.zh: 虽然支持者将这场改革描绘成现代、包容和务实的，但反对者却将其视为仓促、危险的举动，并认为这可能会侵蚀和稀释意大利人的身份认同。

sentences.en: So, what happened? Well, the referendum, in the great tradition of Italian referendums, was declared void after only around 30% of the eligible population turned up to vote.
sentences.zh: 那么，结果如何呢？嗯，延续意大利公投的优良传统，在只有大约30%的有资格人口参与投票后，这次公投被宣布无效。

sentences.en: Of those who voted, around 65% voted to reduce the term limit, with 35% voting against it, but this was to be expected; the Prime Minister, Giorgia Meloni, who was one of the major critics of the proposal, encouraged her supporters to boycott the referendum, so it was hardly surprising that more “yes” supporters turned up to vote than the “no” side.
sentences.zh: 在投票的人中，大约65%的人投票赞成缩短年限，35%的人投票反对，但这也在意料之中；强烈批评该提案的主要推手之一、总理 Giorgia Meloni 鼓励她的支持者抵制这场公投，因此支持“赞成”票的人数多于“反对”阵营也就不足为奇了。

sentences.en: And anyway, legally, a minimum turnout of 50% is required for a referendum to be binding, so the entire thing was declared null and void.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，从法律上讲，公投要具有法律约束力，最低投票率必须达到50%，所以整场公投最终被宣布为无效。

sentences.en: The result was met with cheers by Meloni and her supporters on the right, and with dismay by those who had campaigned for the referendum, who were mainly on the political left.
sentences.zh: 这一结果迎来了 Meloni 及其右翼支持者的欢呼，却让那些为公投奔走呼号、主要来自政治左翼的人士感到沮丧。

sentences.en: Now, without getting too dragged into the topic of Italian politics, I think it’s useful to look at this referendum and the case of Italy as an example of the question of citizenship.
sentences.zh: 好了，在不深入探讨意大利政治的前提下，我认为审视这场公投以及意大利的案例，可以作为一个探讨公民身份问题的典型范例。

sentences.en: What makes one person Italian and another not?
sentences.zh: 究竟是什么让一个人成为意大利人，而另一个人不是？

sentences.en: What does this mean, and what implications does it have for the future of the country?
sentences.zh: 这意味着什么，它对该国的未来又有着怎样的启示？

sentences.en: In the case of Italy, the country has historically had very generous rules on citizenship by ancestry, by descent.
sentences.zh: 就意大利而言，该国历史上对通过世袭、血统获得公民身份的规则一直非常宽容。

sentences.en: In other words, there was a strong preference for the idea that citizenship is something that is passed down from generation to generation, not easily acquired by cultural assimilation.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，它强烈倾向于这样一种观点：公民身份是代代相传的东西，而不是通过文化同化轻易获得的。

sentences.en: In fact, until May of 2025, there were no generational limits for jus sanguinis citizenship.
sentences.zh: 事实上，直到2025年5月，基于血统原则（jus sanguinis）的公民身份在世代上没有任何限制。

sentences.en: Let’s say someone emigrated from Italy in 1861–the year of unification–to America, and they and all of their descendants lived in the US, never setting foot in Italy again and never speaking a word of Italian, and to make it even more dramatic, let’s say they renounced all Italian culture and traditional Italian food, and to make it even worse, their favourite pizza was Hawaiian.
sentences.zh: 假设有人在1861年——即意大利统一那一年——从意大利移民到美国，他和他的所有后代都住在美国，再也没有踏上过意大利的土地，也从不说一句意大利语；为了让情节更戏剧化一点，假设他们摒弃了所有的意大利文化和传统意大利食物，更糟的是，他们最喜欢的披萨竟然是夏威夷披萨。

sentences.en: Their descendant born in 2011, 150 years later, could, if there was an unbroken chain of direct relatives who had claimed Italian citizenship, also apply for Italian citizenship.
sentences.zh: 他们于2011年出生的后代，在150年后，只要有一条由直系亲属构成的、从未中断的曾申领过意大利国籍的链条，也同样可以申请意大利国籍。

sentences.en: If this sounds theoretical, it really isn’t.
sentences.zh: 如果这听起来像是理论上的假设，那可就大错特错了。

sentences.en: An estimated 1.2 million people in Argentina are Italian citizens, including the President, Javier Milei, who has never lived or worked in Italy.
sentences.zh: 据估计，阿根廷有120万意大利公民，其中包括从未在意大利居住或工作过的总统哈维尔·米莱（Javier Milei）。

sentences.en: Now, contrast this with the estimated 2.5 million foreigners who have been living and working in Italy for more than 5 years.
sentences.zh: 现在，将其与估计在意大利生活和工作超过5年的250万外国人进行对比。

sentences.en: The recent referendum was about the question of whether they should have the right to Italian citizenship, and indirectly, whether their children should also become Italian citizens.
sentences.zh: 最近的公投正是围绕他们是否应该拥有获得意大利国籍的权利，以及间接地，他们的孩子是否也应该成为意大利公民这一问题展开的。

sentences.en: To give you an example, let’s say a couple from China have been living and working in Rome for the past 9 years.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，假设一对来自中国的夫妇在过去的9年里一直住在罗马生活和工作。

sentences.en: They have no Italian ancestors or heritage, but they speak fluent Italian, they also have a couple of kids who were born and raised in Italy, and they can correctly tell you what kind of pasta goes with what kind of sauce, and they would never dream of using cream in a carbonara.
sentences.zh: 他们没有意大利祖先或血统，但他们能说流利的意大利语，他们还有几个在意大利出生长大的孩子，他们能准确无误地告诉你哪种面食应该搭配哪种酱汁，而且他们做卡蒂纳里（carbonara）时绝不会做梦去加奶油。

sentences.en: If the referendum had passed, the couple would have been able to apply for Italian citizenship, and their children could become Italian, rather than having to wait until they were 18 to apply.
sentences.zh: 如果公投通过了，这对夫妇将能够申请意大利国籍，他们的孩子也可以成为意大利人，而不必苦等到18岁才能申请。

sentences.en: As you heard, the referendum didn’t pass; it failed badly, and there are even suspicions that there will be another referendum on whether to raise the limit from 10 to 12 years, making it even more difficult to become a citizen by naturalisation.
sentences.zh: 正如你所听到的，公投没有通过；它惨遭失败，甚至有人猜测未来还会有另一场公投，讨论是否将年限从10年提高到12年，从而使通过归化成为公民变得更加困难。

sentences.en: And of course, Italy isn’t the only country grappling with these kinds of questions.
sentences.zh: 当然，意大利并不是唯一一个苦苦应对这类问题的国家。

sentences.en: Take Germany, for example. Up until the year 2000, German citizenship law was based almost entirely on jus sanguinis, on ancestry.
sentences.zh: 以德国为例。直到2000年，德国的国籍法几乎完全基于血统原则（jus sanguinis），也就是血统。

sentences.en: But in 2000, things started to change. Children born in Germany to foreign parents can now receive German citizenship, as long as their parents have been legal residents for a certain period of time.
sentences.zh: 但在2000年，事情开始发生变化。在德国出生的外籍父母的子女现在可以获得德国国籍，只要他们的父母合法居留了一定期限。

sentences.en: And the limit for citizenship by residency was reduced from 15 years to 8, and in 2024, it was reduced again, to 5 years.
sentences.zh: 通过居住获得公民身份的年限从15年缩短到8年，而在2024年，这一年限再次缩短至5年。

sentences.en: In fact, my sister, who lives in Germany, is in the process of becoming a German citizen.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我住在德国的妹妹目前正在办理加入德国国籍的手续。

sentences.en: France, for its part, has long operated under a more inclusive model, with automatic or semi-automatic citizenship for children born in France to foreign parents who have lived in the country.
sentences.zh: 至于法国，长期以来一直奉行更具包容性的模式，对在法国出生且父母长期居住在该国的外国儿童自动或半自动授予国籍。

sentences.en: Even countries like Switzerland, which are traditionally seen as quite restrictive, have gradually eased their naturalisation rules for second-generation immigrants.
sentences.zh: 甚至像瑞士这样传统上被认为相当保守的国家，也逐渐放宽了针对第二代移民的入籍规则。

sentences.en: Italy, by contrast, has held on tightly to the idea that citizenship is primarily something passed down through blood.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，意大利死死抱住“公民身份主要通过血统世代相传”的观念不放。

sentences.en: And in many ways, this reflects the country’s own history.
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，这反映了该国自身的历史。

sentences.en: For most of its modern existence, Italy was a country of emigration, not immigration.
sentences.zh: 在其现代存在的大部分时间里，意大利是一个人口流出国，而不是移民流入国。

sentences.en: Millions of Italians left for North and South America, for Australia, for parts of Europe.
sentences.zh: 数百万意大利人远赴北美、南美、澳大利亚以及欧洲各地。

sentences.en: The Italian state made a conscious choice to maintain legal ties to these people and their descendants, even generations later — hence the extremely generous rules on citizenship by descent.
sentences.zh: 意大利政府有意识地选择与这些人及其后代保持法律联系，哪怕已经过了好几代人——这也是为什么通过血统获得公民身份的规则极其宽容的原因。

sentences.en: But now, as Italy has become a country of immigration, with millions of people from Africa, Asia, Eastern Europe, and the Middle East settling and raising children in the country, this old legal framework is starting to show its cracks.
sentences.zh: 但现在，随着意大利变成了一个移民国家，数百万来自非洲、亚洲、东欧和中东的人在当地定居并养育子女，这个陈旧的法律框架开始显现出裂痕。

sentences.en: And at its core, this is a debate about what citizenship really means.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，这是一场关于公民身份真正含义的辩论。

sentences.en: Is it a legal status passed down from your ancestors, even if you’ve never set foot in the country?
sentences.zh: 它是一个从祖先那里继承下来的法律身份吗，哪怕你从未踏上过这个国家的土地？

sentences.en: Is it a reflection of cultural belonging, of language, school, work, and daily life?
sentences.zh: 它是文化归属感、语言、学校、工作和日常生活的一种反映吗？

sentences.en: Or is it something else entirely, a contract, a symbol of participation, of being part of a shared national project?
sentences.zh: 还是说它是完全不同的其他东西，是一份契约、一种参与的象征、是成为共同国家宏伟蓝图一部分的标志？

sentences.en: In the case of Italy, these questions remain unresolved.
sentences.zh: 就意大利而言，这些问题依然没有答案。

sentences.en: And, if the result of the referendum is anything to go by, they are likely to remain unresolved for some time to come.
sentences.zh: 而且，从公投的结果来看，这些问题在未来一段时间内很可能仍将悬而未决。

sentences.en: OK, then, that is it for today's episode on the question of Italian citizenship.
sentences.zh: 好了，今天的关于意大利公民身份问题的节目就到这里。

sentences.en: To everyone, and especially to the Italians listening, I hope it was an interesting one and that you might have learnt something new.
sentences.zh: 谨向所有人，特别是正在收听节目的意大利听众致意，希望这期节目足够有趣，能让你们学到一些新东西。

sentences.en: As always, I would love to know what you thought of this episode.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，我很想知道你们对这期节目的看法。

sentences.en: What do you think is “the right” way to define who becomes a citizen or not?
sentences.zh: 你认为定义谁能或不能成为公民的“正确”方式是什么？

sentences.en: Do I deserve my Italian citizenship, or is the country handing out passports too liberally?
sentences.zh: 我配得上我的意大利公民身份吗？还是说这个国家发放护照过于慷慨了？

sentences.en: I would love to know, so let’s get this discussion started.
sentences.zh: 我很想知道大家的想法，让我们把这场讨论进行下去吧。

sentences.en: Let me know in the comments below, if you're listening to this somewhere where you can comment, and for the members among you, you can head right into our community forum, which is at community.leonardoenglish.com and get chatting away to other curious minds.
sentences.zh: 如果你在某个可以评论的地方收听此节目，请在下方的评论区告诉我；对于我们会员朋友，你可以直接登录我们的社区论坛 community.leonardoenglish.com，与其他好奇的心灵畅所欲言。

sentences.en: And as a final reminder, this is part one of a three-part mini-series.
sentences.zh: 最后提醒一下，这是三集迷你系列的第第一部分。

sentences.en: Next up we’ll be talking about the Windrush Scandal, and in part three we’ll be looking at a country that wants to keep selling its passports to the highest bidder, and talk about Malta’s battle with the European Union.
sentences.zh: 接下来我们将讨论“疾风世代丑闻”（Windrush Scandal），而在第三部分，我们将关注一个希望继续向出价最高者出售护照的国家，并探讨马耳他与欧盟的博弈。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你刚才收听的是由 Leonardo English 制作的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，请注意安全，我们下期节目见。
